purpose: Measure inside JrubyImportProvider::process_call_node so the next change attaches to a real handler cost, not the provider name on a flamegraph.

instrumentation.mechanism: process-wide AtomicU64 entry counts and per-handler nanosecond sums around the ten call-host steps; PERF log at project_navigation_ready and after_dependencies
instrumentation.overhead_note: Instant::now around every CallNode adds some probe cost; totals are still far below the project phase wall.

run_note: This particular run rebuilt persistent gem products (306 misses); dependency wall is not a warm A/B sample. project_navigation_ready call-host numbers still attribute the project-file path.

after_dependencies.note: Gem fact collection roughly doubles entries; java_ctor becomes the dominant host cost via .new + type inference.

interpretation.verdict: Inside the JRuby call host, project-time cost is only ~0.23s of CPU-sum versus ~5.9s project phase. Samply showed the provider name often, but the door is cheap; most project time is still FactCollector/Prism/other work outside these handlers.
inside_host_ranking_at_project_ready: name-gated import/package/dispatch handlers are ~10–16ms each (mostly enter+name check)
seed sees 150690 dotted candidates but only 258 catalog hits
interpretation.do_not: Optimize call-host scheduling or remove handlers expecting multi-second wins on the project phase.
interpretation.next_measure: Profile FactCollector walk / collect_direct_facts / double AST pass / Prism visitation for the remaining ~5.7s project gap; optionally inspect gem-path java_ctor (~0.5s) as a secondary deps target.
